materials.name: Yellow embossed wallpaper
materials.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: seamless physically based BASE COLOR texture for wallpaper in a first-person liminal office game. Create one square full-bleed texture swatch viewed perfectly straight on, orthographic, of old pale mustard-yellow embossed vinyl wallpaper found in an empty late-1970s office. Fine, restrained vertical meandering pinstripes with tiny elongated diamond / leaf shapes, each only a few centimeters wide in the real material, densely repeating across the swatch. A subtle tactile paper grain and very slight age discoloration; predominantly yellow ochre and straw yellow, with the embossed pattern only slightly darker. The whole swatch represents about 1 meter by 1 meter. It should read as essentially yellow wallpaper at room-view distance, with the woven print visible close up. Natural photographic material detail, subdued pattern contrast, no plaster/concrete patches, no cracks or peeling. BASE COLOR ONLY: diffuse neutral uniform frontal illumination, no directional light or shading, no ambient occlusion, no shadows, no specular highlights, no vignetting, no blur, no fog, no grey veil. Seamlessly repeatable on left/right and top/bottom edges, consistent density across edges, no obvious center motif. Texture fills the entire image edge to edge, no borders, room, architecture, objects, text, symbols, watermark or labels. Output a high-detail square raster texture.

seam_repair.method: Half-tile cyclic offset, built-in image_gen repair of the central seam cross, restoration of the original mean linear RGB, and 24-pixel smooth periodic edge reconciliation. Translation-only repetition; no mirrored or rotated tiles.
seam_repair.edit_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: an existing wallpaper tile cyclically offset by exactly half its width and height for seam repair. There is a visible HORIZONTAL CUT at exactly y=50% and a VERTICAL CUT at exactly x=50%. Repair these two central cut lines: reconnect every interrupted vertical wavy pinstripe and every small leaf/diamond ornament across the horizontal center, and make the background and motifs continuous across the vertical center. Redraw only narrow strips about 5% of image width around this central cross. Preserve ALL surrounding artwork, especially the outer 20% perimeter, exactly; the outer edges already tile correctly and must not change. Keep the same yellow and ochre colors, exposure, fine paper grain, motif sizes, density, positions away from the repaired cross, sharp photographic texture, and flat uniform base-color lighting. No recoloring, yellow saturation boost, smoothing, global redraw, new pattern design, mirror symmetry, reflections or rotations. The objective is invisible repaired joins in the center of this single square swatch. Output the repaired square image at the same size and framing, no border, text, watermark or tiled preview.

flat_field_repair.generator: Built-in image_gen tool with frequency-preserving flat-field postprocessing
flat_field_repair.edit_prompt: Use case: lighting-weather. Asset type: repeating wallpaper PBR BASE COLOR texture, edit of the provided image. Remove ONLY broad uneven illumination and rectangular/square patch contours from the wallpaper background. Make its large-scale background color/exposure spatially uniform in a warm straw/mustard yellow. Keep every fine vertical wavy ochre pinstripe, tiny leaf/diamond motif, its physical size, arrangement, contrast and fine realistic paper grain as closely as possible. This is texture de-lighting / flat-field correction, not new artwork. Eliminate broad light/dark patches, tile-sized panels, box-shaped bands, quadrants, vignettes and gradients. Keep opposite edges seamless with ordinary translation-only repetition. Do not mirror, rotate, add symmetry, blur the fine artwork, redraw motifs, introduce walls/objects/text, change saturation or create directional shadows. Output one square flat uniformly illuminated wallpaper texture swatch matching the source.
flat_field_repair.method: Periodic log-linear RGB frequency separation preserves the existing high-frequency pinstripes, ornaments and paper grain. Broad shading is replaced with 10% of the de-lit reference's low-frequency field; the original arithmetic mean linear RGB is restored. Gaussian approximation sigma 24.5 pixels; four-pixel periodic edge reconciliation. Saved into the PNG; no runtime processing.

center_vertical_repair.method: Masked local inpainting of the vertical seam at x=50%, inserted along minimum-error paths in unchanged context. Original artwork outside columns 505–771 is retained exactly; top/bottom periodicity is reconciled within a 24-pixel edge band.
center_vertical_repair.edit_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: a tall crop from an existing yellow embossed wallpaper texture. The VERTICAL WHITE MASK STRIP at the center marks a defective vertical join to replace. Completely inpaint this white vertical strip with matching wallpaper so there is no vertical seam or distinctive column. Continue the surrounding thin, gently wavy vertical ochre pinstripes and small leaf/diamond ornaments with natural, uniform spacing and the SAME size, rhythm, density, paper grain, warm yellow background, exposure and low contrast. The new pattern must flow naturally across BOTH the left and right boundaries of the filled strip. Do not create a central axis, symmetry, border, doubled stems, a blank yellow stripe, blurry smear or change of color. Keep the already visible artwork on both sides unchanged as closely as possible. The top and bottom of the crop will repeat vertically, so keep their motifs and color in phase and continuous too. This is a local repair of a VERTICAL seam halfway across the original image, not a horizontal seam repair and not a new wallpaper design. No global recoloring, smoothing, mirrors, reflections, rotations, lighting gradients, text, frames, objects, room or perspective. Output the repaired tall rectangular crop with the same framing and proportions.

materials.name: Beige office carpet
materials.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: seamless BASE COLOR texture for beige wall-to-wall office carpet in a first-person liminal office game. Create a square full-bleed overhead orthographic macro photograph of plain short dense cut-pile commercial carpet, the type covering empty late-1970s office floors. Sandy beige, light camel, muted golden tan fibers. Soft irregular fine pile, tightly packed wool/nylon fibers, with subtle natural variation and a few faint wear marks, no large stains. The entire image represents 1 meter by 1 meter of carpet. Realistic individual fine fiber detail at close range; at a distance it must read as a quiet even beige carpet, not tiles, woven fabric, a rug, checkerboard, stripes, braids, stitching or a geometric pattern. Color is warm beige, not gray, green or orange. BASE COLOR ONLY: neutral, completely even diffuse lighting, no directional shadows, no ambient occlusion, no highlights, no baked shading, no depth of field, no fog or vignetting. Perfectly flat view, consistent detail scale, seamlessly repeatable on all four edges. No room, furniture, edges of a rug, border, objects, text, watermark or labels.

materials.name: Warm fine cast concrete
materials.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: one seamless PBR BASE COLOR texture for cast-concrete pedestals in a first-person spatial puzzle game. Primary request: a square, full-bleed, perfectly orthographic photograph of fine smooth cast architectural microconcrete, warm light limestone-beige grey. Represents exactly 0.8 meter by 0.8 meter of real material. Quiet subtle cloudy mineral variation, fine cement grain and sparsely distributed tiny pinhole pores about 0.2 to 1.2 millimeters across; solid cast stone with a matte unpolished finish, delicately visible small details up close but calm uniform material from a distance. Main color warm greige around sRGB #b8b3a3, naturally restrained low contrast, with no yellow ochre tint. No big holes, coarse stones, large aggregate, terrazzo, marble veins, brush strokes, trowel ridges, seams, formwork lines, cracks, scratches, damage, large stains, repeating motifs or directional grain. Uniform flat neutral diffuse frontal illumination, BASE COLOR ONLY, no baked directional shading, no ambient occlusion, shadows, highlights, gradients, vignette or blur. Seamlessly tileable at every edge. Texture fills image edge to edge. No actual pedestal, room, shapes, objects, frame, text, watermark, labels, grid or multiple panels. High resolution detailed square raster.

materials.name: Fine-fissured mineral-fiber office ceiling panel
materials.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: seamless PBR BASE COLOR texture for a single typical suspended office acoustic ceiling panel in a first-person office game. A square full-bleed perfectly orthographic straight-on photograph of the face of a conventional fine-fissured mineral-fiber acoustic ceiling board, the classic plain inexpensive office ceiling material. The entire swatch represents exactly 65 centimeters by 65 centimeters of a real panel. Dense fine chalky mineral fibers, irregular small pinhole pores and many characteristic short thin naturally branching elongated fissures distributed organically in different directions, about 2 to 12 mm long and less than 1 mm wide, with quieter areas between them. Dry matte porous painted mineral fiber, realistic tactile detail, soft warm ivory/off-white around sRGB #ded8bc to match a warm yellow-wallpaper beige-carpet office interior. Fissures should be visibly darker warm grey-beige and read clearly as tiny acoustic pores at close distance, not gigantic cracks. Uniform density, natural nonrepeating arrangement without any dominant motif. BASE COLOR ONLY: completely even neutral diffuse illumination, no directional light, shadows, ambient occlusion, highlights, gradients, vignetting or blur. Seamless tileable edges, edge-to-edge material detail, no panel border, no metal grid, no square pattern, no beveled frame, no seams, no actual room, ceiling scene, perspective, objects, text, labels, watermark or multiple images. No concrete mottling, marble, wood, carpet fibers or large stains. High resolution square raster material photograph.
materials.grid: 24 mm warm greige T-grid (#c9c0ae), slightly darker than the panel, composited at startup in src/materials.ts; same 65 cm grid as square pedestal width, fixtures and pedestal placement

rendering.style_preserved: Original wallpaper and carpet, original warm palette and physical scale

normal_maps.source: Estimated from fine Sobel gradients of the existing albedo in src/material-detail.ts
normal_maps.wrapping: Ordinary repeat without reflections; periodic Sobel gradients across tile boundaries

roughness_maps.source: Estimated from existing albedo at startup

rendering.carpet_finish: MeshPhysicalMaterial sheen 0.25, sheen roughness 0.95; contact shading includes the sheen contribution

concrete_pedestals.finish: Matte fine cast concrete, 0.8 m per tile, JPG base color with estimated linear normal and roughness maps; matching bowls, sharp edges without bevels, original dimensions retained
concrete_pedestals.tint: Half of the original beige tint blended with the untinted concrete in linear RGB, preserving texture variation; neutral uniform darkening inside bowls

rendering.lamp_diffuser: Procedural 512² opal/prismatic diffuser within the existing ceiling fixture
rendering.panel_light: 9 probes per 62.6 cm diffuser filling the opening in a 24 mm T-grid, within a 65 cm ceiling tile; shared dimensions for visible fixtures, lighting bake and PMREM; 55% static diffuse plus 45% live spotlight contribution
rendering.bounce_light: One coarse Lambertian reflection from floor and walls, with room/pedestal visibility; mean material colors

room_lightmaps.calculation: At startup in the existing lighting worker; no per-frame bake

billiard_balls.material: Opaque polished resin, MeshPhysicalMaterial; original red/blue hues and 8 cm diameter
billiard_balls.polish_map: Shared procedural linear roughness texture, 256 squared, mipmapped and anisotropic; no color grain or painted highlights
billiard_balls.contact_shadow: Occupied cups analytically occlude their baked panel illumination with the 4 cm sphere and a panel-sized penumbra; gap-based contact occlusion attenuates indirect and reflected light. A streamed byte attribute changes immediately on pick/place; empty cup color stays uniform.
billiard_balls.reflections: Separate sharp 256-pixel PMREM captured once from the real textured, lit starting room at ball height after materials/light preparation; HDR diffusers included, balls and portal images excluded; shared local approximation without live cube cameras

rendering.environment: Shared soft 128-pixel PMREM for architecture in src/room-environment.ts; sharp 256-pixel actual-scene probe for polished balls in src/scene.ts; both prepared once at startup
